Nurul Amin with Md Aminul Ehsan-For the Petitioner.

parties:
Khadiza Begum ------ Petitioner 
Vs.
Shahjalal Islami Bank Ltd., and another ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
Mahmudul Hoque J: On an application under Article 102 of the Constitution of Bangladesh this Rule Nisi has been issued at the instance of the petitioner calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why Order No. 19 dated 20-9-2011 (Annexure-F) passed by the respondent No.2 in the Artha Rin Execution Case No . 114 of 2010 issuing certificate in favour of the respondent No.1 in respect of the property of the Petitioner should not be declared illegal, without jurisdiction and is of no legal effect and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. Facts relevant for disposal of this Rule Nisi, in brief, are that the land measuring 41 sataks covered by CS Khatian No. 485, SA Khatian No. 16, RS Khatian No. 155 and City Jorip Khatian No. 2431, CS Plot Nos. 701 and 702 and SA Plot Nos. 1270 and 1271 and City Jorip Plot No. 7801 originally belonged to one Moimunnessa, who by a registered Sale Deed No. 4521 dated 17-5-1969 transferred the same to one Mosharraf Hossain. The said Mosharraf Hossain while in possession and enjoyment of the property obtained loan from Agrani Bank, Amin Court Corporate Branch, Dhaka on 3-1-1985 by mortgaging the said property as security against the loan. After the death of said Mosharraf Hossain his heirs redeemed the mortgage by a Deed of Redemption dated 29-3-2010. After redemption by an amicable partition amongst the heirs of Mosharraf Hossain, Md Nazirul Islam got the property in his share. Said Md Nazirul Islam sold 2.65 Kathas or 397 Sataks land out of aforementioned plots to the present Petitioner Khadiza Begum by Deed No. 4845 dated 19-5-2010. The petitioner after purchase constructed a two storied building thereon and residing in the said house. On 17-6-2012 an Officer of the respondent Bank visited the property purchased by the Petitioner and disclosed that the Bank acquired title of the property through Court. On coming to know the said fact the Petitioner by making a search obtained information from the Court concerned and came to know that the respondent Bank obtained an ex-parte Decree by filing Artha Rin Suit No. 45 of 2010 and thereafter by filing Artha Rin Execution Case No. 114 of 2010 obtained a certificate of title under section 33(7) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003("Ain") vide Order No. 19 dated 20-9-2011 and also came to know that the property in question was mortgaged to the respondent No.1 Bank by the petitioner's Vendor vide Mortgage Deed No. 3562 dated 17-7-2003 as second mortgage. It further stated that the Petitioner is the legal owner of the property in question but the respondent No. 1 by practicing fraud obtained an ex-parte Decree and a certificate of title from the Court. The Petitioner is a bonafide purchaser for valuable consideration and she has right to protect her property as a bonafide purchaser without notice of second mortgage. By filing Supplementary Affidavit the petitioner also states that the property in question is situated at Dhaka District but the certificate issued by the Artha Rin Adalat, at Chittagong had no territorial jurisdiction which is in violation of the provisions contained in section 27( 1) of the Ain. At this juncture the petitioner by filing this application challenged the validity and legality of the impugned order and obtained the present Rule and Order of Stay. 

 3. The respondent No.1 Bank contested the Rule by filing an Affidavit-in-Opposition denying all the material allegations made in the writ petition contending, inter alia, that the owner of the property Md Nazirul Islam mortgaged the property to the Bank as security against loan granted to M/s Eastern Accessories Industries a proprietor- ship concern of one Fazlul Haque. The borrower having been failed to pay the loan to the respondent No. 1 Bank, the Bank filed Artha Rin Suit No. 45 of 2010 and obtained an ex-parte Decree against the borrower and the guarantor." Thereafter, the Bank as Decree Holder put the decree into execution by filing Artha Execution Case No. 114 of 2010. In the said Execution Case, the property in question was placed on auction twice under sections 33(4) and (2) of the Ain but no bidder participated in the auction. Finally, the Decree Holder Bank obtained a certificate of title under section 33(7) of the Ain from the Court. While the respondent No. 1 Bank initiated the process for taking over possession of the property, the present petitioner with a view to obstruct the said process filed the instant writ petition and obtained the present Rule and Order of Stay. It is also stated that the Petitioner claimed that she has purchased a portion of the mortgaged property from the mortgagor Md Nazirul Islam on 19-5- 2010 i.e. after creation of mortgage with the Bank and, as such, the transfer is hit by section 530 of the Transfer of Property Act. It is also stated that the Artha Rin Adalat committed no illegality in issuing a certificate vesting the title in the Decree Holder Bank under section 33(7) of the Ain and, as such, the petitioner has no locus standi to challenge the impugned order by invoking writ jurisdiction. 

 4. Mr Nurul Amin, the learned Advocate appearing for the Petitioner submits that the property in question was mortgaged to the Agrani Bank by Mosharraf Hossain who died leaving Md Nazirul Islam and others as heirs. Nazirul Islam redeemed the mortgage from Agrani Bank and after redemption he sold 397 sataks from the said property to the Petitioner on 19-5-2010 and thereafter the Petitioner constructed a two storied building thereon. Mr Amin further submits that the Petitioner being a bonafide purchaser for value is protected by the provision of section 53 of the Transfer of Property Act. It is also argued that the Artha Rin Adalat before issuance of certificate under section 33(7) of the Ain took steps for holding auction twice under section 33(1) and (4). But on both occasions the Adalat failed to company, with the provisions contained in section 33(1) and (4) in its entirety such as beating drum in the locality and affixing of the notice in the Notice Board of the concerned Court as provided in section 33( 1) of the Ain. He also argued that the property situated in Dhaka District but the certificate issued by the Artha Rin Adalat, at Chittagong is in violation of the provision of section 27 of the Ain. He further submits that the Decree Holder Bank cannot directly obtain a certificate under section 33(7) without taking recourse to section 33(5) of the Ain when they took step under section 33(4) and, as such, the impugned order passed by the Adalat issuing a certificate under section 33(7) of the Ain is palpably illegal and without jurisdiction. 

 8. From a plain reading of the aforesaid provision of law it appears that in the event of having a certificate of title under section 33(7) of the Ain the Decree Holder Bank required to follow the provisions of section 33( 1) to (3) and shall refrain from taking any steps under sub-sections (4) and (5). But in the present case the Decree Holder took steps under section 33(4) for holding further auction of the mortgaged property. It is noted that for the purpose of getting a certificate of title under section 33(7) of the A in the law does not enjoin upon a Decree Holder Bank to take step under section 33(4) of the Ain. However, as in the present case when the Bank takes steps under section 33(4) there is no escape route to sidetrack or jump over the provisions of sections 33(5) and (6). The Decree Holder Bank in this situation ought to have invoked the process under section 33(5) of the Ain since the auction have failed and there- after to follow other provisions as contained in section 33(6) of the Ain. Evidently the Decree Holder Bank deviating from that sequential process instead of taking resort to the aforesaid provisions of law straightway applied under section 33(7) of the Ain praying for issuance of the certificate declaring title of the mortgaged property vested in the Bank. This Court finds such invocation of the law to be contrary to the provisions contained in section 33(7) of the Ain. As per provisions of law once the Decree Holder takes steps under section 33(4) for holding further auction there remains no option but to follow the said provision to its statutarioly intended and prescribed 

 9. Since the Artha Rin Adalat issued a certificate directly under section 33(7) of the Ain without allowing prior necessary recourse to the provisions of sections 33(5) and (6) the impugned order passed by the court is found to be illegal. 

 10. Second question raised is whether the Artha Rin Adalat, Chittagong can issue a certificate declaring the title of the property vested in the Decree Holder under section 33(7) of the Ain where the property is situated outside the territorial jurisdiction of the said Court. To meet the question raised, section 27(1) of the Ain may be looked into which runs thus:- 

 11. It appears from the language as used in the above quoted section 27 (1) should the mortgaged property situated beyond the jurisdiction of the Executing Court, it is incumbent upon the Court to send the case to the Court having local jurisdiction for execution of the same. In the present case admittedly the property situated in Dhaka District but the Artha Rin Adalat at Chittagong initiated the process of auction and issued the certificate under section 33(7) of the Ain which is absolutely beyond its territorial jurisdiction as per provision contained in section 27(1). 

 12. In the unreported case of S.Co. Cement Limited represented by its Managing Director vs Artha Rin Adalat No.4, Dhaka (Writ Petition No. 5360 of 2010) a Division Bench of this Court held that: 

 13. Therefore, the certificate issued by the Court indeed, had no jurisdiction and, as such, the issuance of certificate by the Artha Rin Adalat, Chittagong is illegal and without jurisdiction. 

 16. Finally, question raised by the respondent, whether this Court in writ jurisdiction can decide a claim of the petitioner claimant without evidence and who is not a party to the proceedings. 

 17. Admittedly, the petitioner before this Court is not a party to the proceedings. Her case is that she has purchased a little portion of the property from the mortgagor Md Nazirul Islam and is a bonafide purchaser of the mortgaged property for value without notice. 

 18. It is in this context, this Court finds that the Petitioner has remedy under the provisions of Artha Rin Adalat Ain 2003 and an avenue to ventilate her grievance under sections 32 and 33(7kha) and also under sections 38 and 45 of the Ain as the claim of title of the petitioner is not independent of the mortgagor. Moreover, the question of third party claim raised before us is a question off act and requires evidence and enquiry by the Court. In these circumstances this Court is of the view that the petitioner either can settle the dispute amicably out of Court under sections 38 and 45 of the Ain or can take recourse to the relevant provisions of law contained in the Ain by filing an appropriate application before the Artha Rin Adalat, if so advised. 

 19. With the above observations this Court is inclined to dispose of this Rule 

 22. The Artha Rin Adalat directed to transfer the Artha Jari Case to the competent Court having territorial jurisdiction as per provisions of section 27(1) of the Ain. The respondent Bank shall be at liberty to proceed with the Execution Case before the transferee Court by taking steps under section 33(1) on wards. The transferee Court is also directed to dispose of the case within a shortest time possible after receipt of the case from the transferor Court. 

 23. The Order of Stay granted at the time of issuance of this Rule by this Court is, hereby, recalled and vacated. 

 Communicate a copy of the judgment to the Court concerned forthwith.
